record.text: Me gusta mucho el duende.
record.notes: The father's running example. duende = the mysterious power of art to move (Lorca, flamenco), also 'goblin'; gusta = the thing pleases me (gustar construction), and the verb is related to taste. Validation (§6.3) checks that the leftover orders duende > gusta > mucho.

record.text: Sinto muita saudade da casa da minha avó.
record.notes: Aching longing for something absent; the word-level runs' lead case.

pt_saudade.text_B1: I miss my grandmother's house a lot.

record.text: Nos quedamos de sobremesa hasta que anocheció.
record.notes: Unhurried after-meal conversation at the table; 'quedarse de sobremesa' is also a fixed expression.

es_sobremesa.text_B1: We stayed for after-dinner chat until it grew dark.

record.text: Jeden Herbst packt mich das Fernweh.
record.notes: Longing for faraway places (the opposite of homesickness); 'packt mich' = seizes me.

de_fernweh.text_B1: Every autumn, I get the travel bug.

record.text: Porta quel vestito con una certa sprezzatura.
record.notes: Studied nonchalance that hides effort (Castiglione).

it_sprezzatura.text_B1: Wear that dress with a certain nonchalance.

record.text: Magari passo da te stasera, vediamo.
record.notes: magari as 'maybe, perhaps, if things work out'. Its wish use ('if only') is in it_magari_wish (construction).

it_magari_forse.text_B1:
Perhaps I'll pass by you tonight, see you. (Informal)

or

Perhaps I'll stop by you tonight, let's see. (Formal)

record.text: Ele deu um jeitinho e conseguiu o documento no mesmo dia.
record.notes: Brazilian 'jeitinho': finding a creative, often rule-bending way round an obstacle.

pt_jeitinho.text_B1: He found a way and managed to get the document on the same day.

record.text: Ela fazia cafuné no filho até ele dormir.
record.notes: Brazilian 'cafuné': tenderly running your fingers through someone's hair.

pt_cafune.text_B1: She was combing her son's hair until he fell asleep.

record.text: In der kleinen Hütte herrschte eine wunderbare Gemütlichkeit.
record.notes: Warmth, cosiness, belonging, unhurried good cheer.

de_gemuetlichkeit.text_B1: A wonderful coziness reigned in the little cottage.

record.text: Endlich Feierabend, gehen wir noch ein Bier trinken?
record.notes: The end of the working day, and the free time and mood that begin then.

de_feierabend.text_B1: Shall we go for a beer after work, finally?

record.text: À Tokyo, j'ai ressenti un profond dépaysement.
record.notes: The disorientation (pleasant or not) of being out of your own country or element.

fr_depaysement.text_B1: In Tokyo, I felt a profound homesickness.

record.text: Les retrouvailles avec mes cousins ont été très émouvantes.
record.notes: The joy of being reunited after a long separation; a plural noun with no English singular equivalent.

fr_retrouvailles.text_B1: The reunions with my cousins were very touching.

record.text: A mi hermana le gustan las películas de terror.
record.notes: The films please my sister (the experiencer is the indirect object; the verb agrees with the films).

record.text: Mi manchi tanto, lo sai?
record.notes: "You are missing to me": the person missed is the subject, the one who misses is the indirect object.

it_mi_manchi.text_B1: You miss me a lot, don't you?

record.text: Se me olvidó el paraguas en el tren.
record.notes: Accidental "se": the umbrella forgot itself on me (no blame on the speaker).

es_se_me_olvido.text_B1: I forgot my umbrella on the train.

record.text: Mir ist kalt, kannst du das Fenster zumachen?
record.notes: "To me it is cold": a dative experiencer, not "I am cold".

de_mir_ist_kalt.text_B1: Are you cold too? Can you close the window?

record.text: La película es aburrida, y yo estoy aburrido.
record.notes: ser/estar: "boring" vs "bored"; English uses "be" for both.

es_ser_estar.text_B1: The movie is boring, and I am bored.

record.text: Il me faut encore une heure pour finir.
record.notes: Impersonal necessity with a dative ("it is needed to me").

fr_il_me_faut.text_B1: I need one more hour to finish.

record.text: Comprei o livro para lermos juntos.
record.notes: The Portuguese personal (inflected) infinitive, "for us-to-read".

pt_infinitivo_pessoal.text_B1: I bought the book to read together.

record.text: Magari fosse già venerdì!
record.notes: magari + imperfect subjunctive as a wish ("if only"). Pairs with it_magari_forse.

it_magari_wish.text_B1: If only it were already Friday!

record.text: No te creo, me estás tomando el pelo.
record.notes: "You are taking my hair": you are pulling my leg.

es_tomar_el_pelo.text_B1: I don't believe you, you're pulling my leg.

record.text: Domani hai l'esame? In bocca al lupo!
record.notes: "Into the wolf's mouth": good luck (the reply is "crepi", may it die).

it_in_bocca_al_lupo.text_B1: Tomorrow do you have an exam? Good luck!

record.text: Depuis qu'il pleut, j'ai le cafard.
record.notes: "I have the cockroach": I feel down or blue.

fr_cafard.text_B1: Since it's raining, I feel gloomy.

record.text: Hast du Tomaten auf den Augen? Die Ampel ist rot!
record.notes: "Tomatoes on your eyes": you are not seeing the obvious.

de_tomaten.text_B1: Do you have tomatoes on your eyes? The traffic light is red!

record.text: Estou com saudades de você.
record.notes: "I am with saudades of you": I miss you. A fixed phrase built on an untranslatable (compare pt_saudade).

record.text: Mi hijo siempre está en las nubes en clase.
record.notes: "Is in the clouds": daydreaming, absent-minded.

es_en_las_nubes.text_B1: My son is always in the clouds in class. (This idiomatic expression means that my son is always daydreaming or not paying attention in class.)

record.text: La nuova collega è proprio in gamba.
record.notes: "In leg": capable, smart, on the ball.

it_in_gamba.text_B1: The new colleague is quite agile.

record.text: Elle m'a posé un lapin hier soir.
record.notes: "She put a rabbit on me": she stood me up.

fr_poser_un_lapin.text_B1: She put a rabbit on me yesterday evening.

record.text: El tren sale a las ocho de la mañana.

es_tren.text_B1: The train departs at eight in the morning.

record.text: Mi hermana vive en una casa pequeña.

es_casa.text_B1: My sister lives in a small house.

record.text: Ich habe zwei Brüder und eine Schwester.

de_brueder.text_B1: I have two brothers and a sister.

record.text: Das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch in der Küche.

de_tisch.text_B1: The book is on the table in the kitchen.

record.text: Il negozio chiude alle sette di sera.

it_negozio.text_B1: The store closes at seven in the evening.

record.text: Mio padre beve un caffè ogni mattina.

it_caffe.text_B1: My father drinks a coffee every morning.

record.text: O médico chegou ao hospital às nove horas.

pt_medico.text_B1: The doctor arrived at the hospital at nine o'clock.

record.text: Comprei pão e leite no mercado.

pt_mercado.text_B1: I bought bread and milk at the market.

record.text: Le chat dort sur le canapé rouge.
record.notes: probe is canapé, not chat (English 'chat' would trigger the source-word masking).

fr_chat.text_B1: The cat is sleeping on the red sofa.

record.text: Nous avons visité le musée avec nos enfants.

fr_musee.text_B1: We visited the museum with our children.

record.text: cominceranno a ddì: ffora a cchi ttoca.
record.notes: "Out, whoever's turn it is!", the trumpeting angels calling the dead out. Belli line 4.
record.source: Belli, Er giorno der giudizzio, line 4 (web edition)

rom_ffora.text_B1:
Commencersont à parler : sortez ceux qui touchent. (French)

They will start to speak: let those who are touched come out. (English)

record.text: de schertri da la terra a ppecorone,
record.notes: schertri = skeletons; a ppecorone = on all fours. Both models misread schertri as "jesters" in the lattice run. Belli line 6.
record.source: Belli, Er giorno der giudizzio, line 6 (web edition)

rom_schertri.text_B1: From the earth to the cheese, [it] travels.
